titleText.es: Algún ingeniero de por ahí ha resuelto el problema P=NP y está enzarzado en una rutina de calibración de una batidora eléctrica. Por cada 0x5f375a86 que descubrimos, hay miles que no vemos.
titleText.en: Some engineer out there has solved P=NP and it's locked up in an electric eggbeater calibration routine.  For every 0x5f375a86 we learn about, there are thousands we never see.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish archive and official xkcd source both identify comic #664. The Spanish title text translates the official examples of important discoveries hidden in routine engineering. The raster supplies both large branch bubbles that OCR missed, joins the line-broken PÁRRAFO, and keeps 48, 200, and OUTLOOK as nonlexical source units.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Pasaron is the completed-past they-form of pasar. With a recipient such as me and an object, pasar can mean to hand or give that object to someone.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; begins por casualidad
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Por combines with casualidad to mean that something happened by chance.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: in; within (the time taken to finish)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Before a duration, en can state how much time an action took to complete.

example.es: Terminé el informe en dos horas.
example.en: I finished the report in two hours.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Resuelto is the irregular completed-action form of resolver; it appears with haber in forms such as he resuelto.

example.en: I have already solved the problem.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Supondrá is the future form of suponer for one thing. Here it introduces the consequences something will bring.

example.en: The change will entail more work.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Tesis has the same written form in the singular and plural; surrounding words show the number.

example.es: Leyó dos tesis sobre el tema.
example.en: She read two theses on the topic.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: In teoría de colas, colas are mathematical waiting lines studied in systems where jobs or people wait for service.

example.es: La teoría de colas ayuda a modelar esperas.
example.en: Queueing theory helps model waiting times.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Conseguido is the completed-action form of conseguir. With has and a que-clause, it asks whether the listener has managed to bring about another result.

example.en: Have you managed to get it to work?

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Deje is a special form of dejar used after conseguir que because the stopping is a result someone is trying to bring about. Ordinary deja changes to deje.

example.en: I want it to stop raining.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; marks sincronizarse, to synchronize
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Se presents the program as becoming synchronized with something else rather than directly synchronizing an object.
Sincronice is the special form of sincronizar used after hacer que because synchronization is the result being caused. Ordinary sincroniza changes to sincronice.

example.es: Haz que el reloj se sincronice.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: In combinations such as ir lento, lento describes how an action or process runs. It stays masculine singular because it describes the action rather than a noun.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that something happened by chance or unexpectedly?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Por stays fixed and casualidad names chance. The expression can modify an action directly or appear in questions where English might say “by any chance.”

example.en: I found the key by chance.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say approximately or exactly half a dozen of something?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use media docena de, then name what is counted.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Media agrees with the feminine noun docena and means half. Docena stays singular here, and de introduces the counted thing; only the later noun normally changes for plural meaning.

example.en: We bought half a dozen eggs.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: What common Spanish phrase means a textbook?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use libro de texto; use libros de texto for more than one.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Libro is the main noun and carries the plural ending. De texto classifies the book's use and stays unchanged in the plural.

example.es: Necesito un libro de texto nuevo.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: Why do the two workplaces react so differently to the same programming breakthrough?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: The joke contrasts academic incentives to publish and teach a discovery with a company's narrow interest in whether its immediate software task now works.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The hidden breakthrough is treated as potentially important research in the academic branch, while the business branch evaluates it only as routine performance and compatibility work. The official title text sharpens the joke by suggesting that major theoretical discoveries may remain buried inside ordinary engineering code.

applications.explanationEn: Empresarial follows mundo because it classifies the kind of world or sphere being named.
Empresarial has one singular form for both masculine and feminine nouns, so it agrees with singular mundo without changing its ending.
Has is the present helper for one familiar listener, and conseguido is conseguir's completed-action form.

applications.exampleEs: HAS CONSEGUIDO QUE EL PROGRAMA DEJE
applications.explanationEn: Has conseguido supplies the completed managed action, que introduces the other action, and deje is dejar's special caused-result form.
Deje changes to fit the managed result, de is the required link, and ir stays in its unchanged dictionary form as the action that stops.
Hacer que introduces the caused result, and sincronice is sincronizar's special caused-action form.
Nuestros takes masculine plural -os because it matches the masculine plural noun móviles.
Lento describes the slow manner of ir, so it stays in the fixed masculine singular form rather than agreeing with programa.
Nuevos comes before móviles to present the phones as newly added or recent, rather than emphasizing that they were newly manufactured.
Nuevos uses masculine plural -os to match móviles.
